title: A separate regime for the largest projects
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: Let the planning cohort answer whether the regime has delivered on its intent. They will have covered the UK system in detail and this is the moment to use that.
text: A separate regime for the largest projects The Planning Act 2008 created a distinct consenting route for nationally significant infrastructure: airports above a threshold, major roads and railways, large generating stations, and similar. Rather than a local planning application, the promoter applies for a Development Consent Order, which is examined by an appointed panel and decided by the Secretary of State. The design intent was to make decisions on projects of national importance faster and more predictable by separating the question of principle, settled in advance through a National Policy Statement, from the question of detail, settled in the examination. Whether it has achieved that is a live argument, and one the planning students will have met in PGR01. G PGR01 Michaelmas lectures 3 and 4. 83

title: The Development Consent Order process
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: The last row is the one investors care about most and it is where the Heathrow story turns. Confirm the current statutory timetable before teaching, as it has been amended.
text: The Development Consent Order process G Planning Act 2008 and subsequent amendments. Statutory periods to be confirmed before delivery. 84 Stage What happens Why it matters to an investor Policy A National Policy Statement establishes the need case and the principle The question of whether to build is settled before the application, which removes the largest single risk Pre-application Statutory consultation with communities and statutory bodies Long, expensive, and the stage where the scheme is actually shaped Acceptance and examination An Examining Authority runs a written and hearing-based process to a statutory timetable A defined timetable is what makes the regime financeable at all Recommendation and decision The Examining Authority reports and the Secretary of State decides A political decision at the end of a quasi-judicial process Challenge Judicial review of the decision or of the policy statement behind it The residual risk. A consent is final only once the courts are finished

title: Heathrow expansion as a case in state and private partnership
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: This is the framing paragraph for the guest session. It says why the case is worth the hour without pre-empting what the speaker will say. Update once the 11 September call has happened.
text: Heathrow expansion as a case in state and private partnership Heathrow expansion is an unusually complete case for this week. The need case was settled through a national policy statement rather than a planning application. That statement was itself challenged in the courts, found unlawful at one level and reinstated at another, which is a demonstration that the policy stage carries litigation risk and not only the decision stage. The scheme is promoted by a privately owned airport operator whose charges are regulated by the Civil Aviation Authority, so the return on the investment depends on a regulatory determination that is separate from the consent. And the government’s position has changed with governments. Every element of this week is present in one project: policy, consent, regulation, litigation, and a state that is simultaneously the planning authority, the economic regulator, the policy-maker and, in effect, a commercial counterparty. G Case detail to be confirmed with the Department for Transport before delivery. 85

title: What a national policy statement settles, and what it does not
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: The risk transfer point is the finance-facing reading of a planning instrument, and it is the sort of translation this module exists to do.
text: What a national policy statement settles, and what it does not A national policy statement establishes the need for a category of infrastructure and the policy against which individual applications will be judged. Its purpose is to take the argument about whether the country needs, say, additional airport capacity out of the examination of a particular scheme, so that the examination can be about that scheme. That is a genuine transfer of risk from the promoter to the state, and it is the main reason the regime is financeable. It is also why the policy statement, rather than the consent, has become the object of litigation: challenge the policy and every application resting on it falls with it. G Planning Act 2008; PGR01 Michaelmas lecture 4. 86

title: What the litigation history teaches
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: This is the strongest environmental policy link in the week, and the EP students will know the climate litigation material well. Let them explain the grounds and then ask the finance students what it does to a discount rate.
text: What the litigation history teaches A policy statement can be quashed for a failure of process rather than for being substantively wrong, and the distinction matters to an investor only in that a process failure can usually be cured. Climate obligations have become a live ground of challenge for high-emitting infrastructure, which converts a policy commitment into a legal constraint on consenting. Litigation adds years, and years at the pre-construction stage are expensive because the equity is committed and earning nothing. A promoter cannot insure against this, and cannot easily price it, which is why policy risk is the risk most often cited by investors as the reason they will not fund greenfield infrastructure. The remedy, if there is one, is a policy framework robust enough to survive challenge rather than a faster court. G EP01 Lent week 7, international climate change litigation; EP07 week 4, adjudication systems. 87

title: Surface access, and the coordination problem
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: A good question for the guest: how is that dependency actually managed, and what happens when the complementary scheme slips.
text: Surface access, and the coordination problem A major airport expansion depends on road and rail capacity that the promoter does not control and cannot build. That capacity is funded by a different department, appraised under a different business case, and delivered on a different timetable, and its benefits are shared with users who have nothing to do with the airport. This is the coordination institution in PIMA, and its failure is one of the most common reasons infrastructure underdelivers. A scheme appraised on the assumption that complementary investment arrives, where nothing obliges anyone to provide it, has embedded an assumption it cannot enforce. G IMF PIMA, coordination between entities; PGR05 lecture 4, regional accessibility and investment in transportation infrastructure. 88

title: Where the state meets the private partner
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: The last card is not a criticism, it is the structural fact that makes this week necessary. The state is not a single actor and its parts have different objectives.
text: Where the state meets the private partner As policy-maker Setting the national policy statement that establishes whether the project should happen at all, and revising it when policy changes. As consenting authority Running the examination and taking the decision, through a process that must be, and must be seen to be, procedurally fair. As economic regulator Determining the charges the operator may levy, and therefore whether the investment earns a return, through a separate process on a separate timetable. As guarantor of surface access Delivering the road and rail capacity the scheme depends on, which is a different department with its own budget and its own appraisal. As climate policy-maker Setting the carbon budgets against which the scheme’s emissions are assessed, which is what made the policy statement litigable. As a party with an interest Wanting the investment to happen for growth reasons, while running the processes that decide whether it may. G 89

title: Questions to put to the guest
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
notes: Send these to the speaker in advance. Questions three and four are the ones an academic audience would not think to ask and a practitioner can answer better than anyone.
text: Questions to put to the guest Where in the process does a scheme of this kind actually get decided, as opposed to where the statute says it is decided? How does a promoter manage a consenting process that outlasts several governments and their policies? What can be committed to a private partner before consent is granted, and what has to wait? How is the interaction between the consent timetable and the regulatory determination managed, given that neither can wait for the other? What would you change about the regime, and what is good about it that outsiders miss? G 90

title: Block G discussion
blockname: Heathrow and nationally significant infrastructure
text: Block G discussion Seminar questions The Development Consent Order regime settles the principle in advance through a policy statement. What risk does that transfer, from whom to whom? Heathrow expansion has been supported, refused, litigated and revived. What would a rational investor have done at each turn, and what does that imply about the cost of policy instability? The state appears in this case as policy-maker, consenting authority, regulator, infrastructure provider and interested party. Is that a problem to be solved or a fact to be managed? G 91

title: Where Week 2 leaves us
blockname: Reserve material
notes: Four sentences, one per block group. If students remember only these, week 2 has done its work.
text: Where Week 2 leaves us The case for state involvement rests on four market failures, and none of them says whether the state should own, regulate or contract. Selection is where the value is made or lost, and the institutions that select are the subject rather than the background. A price control is a weighted average cost of capital set administratively, which converts market risk into political risk rather than removing it. The competition that precedes a concession is undone by the renegotiation that follows it, unless the institutions to prevent that were built first. 96
